page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-4 is a memory-oriented virtual machine configuration within the N1 machine series. It features 4 virtual CPUs derived from 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz using the x86_64 architecture. The instance includes 26.0 GB of system memory, providing 6.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is not bundled, requiring network-attached persistent disks for all non-volatile storage needs, and the instance includes no discrete hardware accelerators or GPUs.

In benchmark assessments, the older Intel architecture yields modest compute and throughput scores across standard test suites. The instance achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 924.0 and a multi-core score of 2032.0, both placing in the lower percentiles relative to modern compute platforms. Stress-ng scores register at 1109.89 for single-core and 2914.17 for multi-core processing. Large-block uncached memory bandwidth reaches 25.86 GB/s for reads and 21.97 GB/s for writes, supporting baseline memory operations while trailing modern high-bandwidth architectures. Redis SET performance achieves 2.75 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput measures 2.82 GB/s.

The primary architectural tradeoff of the n1-highmem-4 is its legacy compute baseline paired with an elevated memory allocation. Workloads constrained by CPU processing or AVX-512 instruction requirements will encounter throughput limitations, as the processor supports standard AVX and AES but lacks AVX-512 extensions. The configuration is primarily appropriate for memory-demanding legacy applications, intermediate in-memory caching layers, medium-scale relational databases, and background ETL tasks that require moderate RAM headroom without high per-core computational demands.
description: Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-4 is a virtual machine designed for memory-intensive workloads requiring dedicated CPU allocation. Based on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an Intel Xeon processor operating at 2.3 GHz with 4 vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores. The instance features 26.0 GB of system RAM, delivering 6.5 GB of memory per vCPU, while offering no bundled local storage and no GPU acceleration. Benchmark results reflect legacy CPU performance, with Geekbench scores of 924.0 single-core and 2032.0 multi-core, alongside uncached memory read bandwidth of 25.86 GB/s. Redis throughput reaches 2.75 million operations per second. While computational density and instruction set capabilities are modest compared to newer generation hardware, the configuration offers substantial memory capacity relative to core count. It is suitable for in-memory caching, mid-sized relational database hosting, and lightweight data processing pipelines where memory capacity outweighs raw compute throughput.
